text:
jay: Heads-up — we started seeing a p99 latency regression for model lynxprime after the tokenizer v2 rollout. Spike is specific to long inputs (>8k tokens). p95 also up but p99 is noisy. Started ~09:12 UTC when onboarding traffic ramped.

jay: Quick numbers from infra dashboard: baseline p99 ~420ms, current p99 ~1.8s for requests with long context. p95 moved from ~220ms -> ~680ms. Hosted route: /v1/generate model=lynxprime-2026-03-10

jay: Repro (from prod-like env):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"lynxprime-2026-03-10","input":"<~9k token doc>","max_tokens":256}'
```

ingrid: @jay :eyes: can you paste a sample payload (non-sensitive) and the rough token counts? also which kernel/hardware fleet is this hitting?

jay: Sample attached (redacted). Long text is ~9.1k tokens. This route mostly hits eu-west-2 fleet (A100-p4d pool) via smart-routing policy.

evan: I pulled traces — most time is in pre-tokenize + tokenize slowpath and then a KV cache invalidation step. Trace snippet: 
```
tokenizer: slow path fallback (subword resegmentation) 450ms
kvcache: invalidate(prefix) ~220ms
serve: model forward 180ms
```
The tokenizer v2 change added a unicode normalization pass which seems to trigger slowpath for large contiguous segments.

maria: Is this only for lynxprime or seen in other new models?

evan: So far only lynxprime onboarding traffic. We have a hypothesis: tokenizer v2 heuristics cause unexpected subtoken churn on long inputs (esp. with mixed CJK + emoji sequences), leading to resegmentation and higher memory churn which then increases KV cache churn/invalidation.

ops-bot: [alert] Lynxprime p99 latency > 1.5s threshold (10:03 UTC) — autoscaler did not breach, but routing fallback started hitting older model variants.

ingrid: Immediate mitigation options: 1) pin customer routes to lynxprime-2026-03-09 (previous tokenizer compat) 2) temporarily enable prefix KV caching for long-context (increase TTL) 3) throttle onboarding ramp for lynxprime 4) rollback tokenizer v2 for the model. Which do we want to try first?

jay: Let's try 1 + 3: pin affected customers to previous version and cut onboarding ramp by 50% for next 30 mins. I can push a routing change now.

maria: I'm going to file a customer notification and update the status page. Tagging impacted accounts list from the onboarding run.

evan: I'll instrument the tokenizer to log fallback counts and add a sample histogram metric. If we can show fallback rate correlates to p99, eng-ml can iterate heuristics.

ingrid: After pinning we saw p99 drop to ~490ms within two ramping cycles. p95 back to ~260ms. Looks like a successful short-term mitigation.

jay: Confirmed with quick smoke tests — pinned version baseline is fine. Will keep routing pin for 2 hours and then re-evaluate after eng-ml patch.

evan: Next actions: create ENG-ML ticket with trace links, tokenizer fallback logs, and a small repro corpus. Proposed fixes: optimize unicode normalization path, add early fast-path checks for contiguous runs, and avoid resegmentation for certain chunk patterns.

maria: I'll open SUPPORT-7923 to track customer comms + credits if needed.

ingrid: Ops note: consider adding an alert for tokenizer-swap delta (sudden increase in fallback rate) — would catch future rollouts faster.

jay: Thanks everyone. I'll post follow-up when ENG-ML has a patch. For now pinned and throttled. :thumbsup:
